scenes.headline: Faster Typing Is Still Zero Leverage
bullets: Most people treat AI like a slightly faster typewriter
Manual prompting all day still chains output to your hours
scenes.narration: Most people use AI like a faster typewriter. They sit inside a chat window all afternoon trading manual typing for manual prompting.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)

scenes.headline: Henry Ford's 1913 Assembly Line Divide
bullets: Ford did not just hand mechanics faster wrenches
He sequenced every step into a deterministic system
scenes.narration: In 1913, Henry Ford did not hand mechanics faster wrenches - he engineered a repeatable assembly line. Today, solo operators face that exact same divide with digital work.
scenes.source: Ford Motor Company, moving assembly line at Highland Park (1913)

scenes.headline: One-Off Chatting vs Documented SOP Engines
scenes.left_body: Blank chat box -> re-explain rules daily -> inconsistent
scenes.right_body: Fixed Input -> Quality Checklist -> Locked Output
scenes.narration: Chatting one prompt at a time keeps you trapped as the bottleneck. Building a workflow turns one documented standard operating procedure into a pipeline that runs on raw inputs.

scenes.headline: The 3-Block Workflow Specification
scenes.stat_subtext: Repeat 3x -> Lock Input, Rules & Output Template
scenes.narration: Apply the Three-Block Rule: whenever you repeat a digital task three times, stop chatting and write a fixed spec - exact input format, strict quality checklist, and a locked output template.

scenes.headline: Architect the Pipeline Once, Feed It Ideas
scenes.stat_label: ONE SPEC REPLACES A HUNDRED CHATS
bullets: Stop improvising prompts from scratch every morning
Build modular Input -> Process -> Output assets
scenes.narration: Amateurs write clever prompts from scratch; owners design pipelines once and feed them raw ideas. And until you make that shift...
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
